fixes.explanation: Josiah son of Zephaniah, that's the house. Zechariah is told to go there that same day. The text gives us the name and that instruction, and that's all it gives. I'll leave it right there, friend.

Hilkiah son of Shallum shows up in a list of priests' families (1 Chronicles 6:13), but he's not in this passage. The text tells Zechariah to go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah. Names come in bunches here, and it's easy to grab the one from another list. I've mixed up a name or two myself, and I had a handle with mine carved in it.

A city is a big job, but that's not what the verse says. The Branch will build the temple of the LORD. Verse 13 says it again: "Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD…" It's the same building, said twice.

An altar is a good guess, since it's a holy thing too. But the text says the Branch will build the temple of the LORD. The verse never mentions an altar. Stick close to what's written, friend, and the answer is right there.

A shepherd is a fair guess, and David is called a shepherd of God's people (2 Samuel 5:2). But this verse doesn't use that word for the Branch. It says the Branch will be a priest on His throne. Stick close to what's written, friend, and the answer is right there.

This one's false, friend. God doesn't say anything about a rivalry. The verse says, "…there will be peaceful counsel between the two." The Branch rules and is a priest on His throne, and the text calls it peaceful.

False is right. Nobody's squaring up here. The text says, "…there will be peaceful counsel between the two." He rules and He's a priest on His throne, and the word is peaceful. Friend, no rivalry anywhere in that verse.
True. Verse 15 says, "Even those far away will come and build the temple of the LORD…" So the building reaches the ones who are far away. That's a big circle, friend.

Obey, you got it. The last line says, "This will happen if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God." Notice the word diligently. It means this obeying is no half-hearted nod, and I've nodded along at my oven timer plenty of times.
